grades.Strong: At least 2 meta-analyses or systematic reviews, the largest (or all the trials together) covering at least 1,000 participants, and at least 80 % of the evidence pointing the same way.
grades.Moderate: At least 1 meta-analysis or systematic review, or at least 3 randomised trials, covering at least 300 participants, with at least two-thirds of the evidence pointing the same way.
grades.Limited: At least two-thirds of the evidence points the same way, but there are too few or too small studies for Moderate.
grades.Mixed: The studies point different ways: no finding carries two-thirds of the evidence.
grades.Insufficient: No meta-analysis or systematic review and fewer than 2 randomised trials, or the studies do not say clearly what they found.

rubric.weighting: Each meta-analysis or systematic review counts as 3 trials when we weigh which way the evidence points. Studies whose abstract does not say clearly what they found are left out. A grade says how settled a finding is, whichever way it points: consistent reviews that found no clear difference can grade Strong.
